headline: Dry, steadily milder weather lasts through Saturday, then a storm could bring heavy rain, possibly several inches, sometime Sunday into Monday, though its track is still very uncertain.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Strong high pressure keeps New York City and the surrounding area dry and clear on Tuesday and Tuesday night. Northwest to west winds run around 12 mph this afternoon, easing to about 6–8 mph tonight in the city and along the coast and going light to calm in the outlying suburbs. With clear skies and light winds, tonight's low will depend on how efficiently the ground cools off, so outlying spots will run colder than the city.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Wednesday through Friday stay dry and clear as the high pressure slowly settles over the area, with light west to west-northwest winds of about 6–9 mph on Wednesday. Temperatures keep warming, with highs reaching the upper 50s to mid 60s on Thursday and Friday. Nights stay chilly through Thursday morning under clear, calm skies, but starting Thursday night a southwest breeze brings in a bit more moisture, so lows won't drop as far.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday looks dry with the milder nights continuing. By Sunday, a disturbance approaches from the northwest while a separate system from the subtropics may spin up a storm that moves up the East Coast, with a decent chance of a period of moderate to locally heavy rain Sunday into Monday and the possibility of several inches in 24 hours somewhere near the area. Newer AI-based forecast models more consistently take the storm farther west, which would bring steadier rain, while the main traditional global models (the European and American) take it farther east and could largely miss the area; the exact timing and how the two systems merge will decide which happens.

coast: Calm boating conditions through the week with no advisories: winds mostly from the northwest to west under 15 knots (about 17 mph) and ocean seas no higher than 2–3 feet.
watch_for: Whether the Sunday–Monday storm tracks close to the coast (steady, possibly heavy rain with several inches possible) or stays offshore and mostly misses.
Possible poor visibility and low clouds in rain on Sunday if the storm comes close.
confidence: High confidence in dry, gradually warming weather through Saturday; low confidence in the timing, track and rain totals for the Sunday–Monday storm.
